item.title: The Candy Cane: The Candy Cane
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror and History

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: The SCP I envisioned is a plastic candy cane filled with small M&M-like candies that have different outcomes to it. While one candy that was eaten will give a person something like a lost possession or make them feel happy another could have immense tragedy or have the person who ate it either die or vanish through a trans dimensional entry way or property while a small select few saying that they are speaking for the candy cane.

Central Narrative: The story is mainly about how the candies affected history and while they test the object it shows some form of sentience and claims to have caused some of the worst tragedies and triumphs in history and saying that they had been the first thing consumed and will be the last thing consumed by man.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is just an idea that I had and wanted to share. While some SCP’s are intriguing for their gruesome nature and such I think an SCP that is more based on luck and a way to solve some of the worlds greater mysteries and why certain things happened would be a intriguing idea.

Additional Notes: I just have a problem of answering a genre. However, I am pretty confident in this even with a hiccup in that department. I will except all the feedback I can get because this one I want to see through till the end and make this my first SCP entry.

item.title: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded: I really like the idea here, I think it's pretty unique, but I'm a little confused with how the immortality and multiple identities work. You say the scp is impossible to kill, but can die. Does this mean that it is impervious to any weapons, but can die from old age or disease? and in that case, does it just live a normal human life span until dying and being reincarnated as one of the 10 different forms? If that is how it works, I think a cool idea to add would be that within each of its life spans, it, as you describe, goes from asking for basic supplies, to more extreme mediums, and at the end of each life span it attempts to do something SUPER dangerous and the foundation has to do something to stop it each time. I'm not sure how dangerous art could be lol, but maybe you could think of something.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Fireproof SAR Dog: Re: Seeking Greenlight: Fireproof SAR Dog
item.content:encoded: Right now, I’m not getting what I should really be paying attention to in this story. Is it the anomalous abilities themselves? Is it the fire department this dog was working for? You mention in the beginning that this dog can control small fires, but you never bring that up again. I don’t know if talking about SAR missions where a dog happened to be safe would really be interesting. here’s a guide that I think explains the problem I’m seeing. I’ll paraphrase a bit. Right now you have a very simple anomaly, which is fine, but you’re going to want to add a bit more depth if you really want to grab the reader’s attention. That being said, you do actually have certain directions you can go with this. If you want to focus on the SAR part of this then you might want to expand on the dog’s powers some more. If you want to focus on the dog itself then you might want to show the extent of its abilities, maybe throw some logical extremes in there. There’re of course other paths you can take with this, those are just two ways to go.

item.title: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
All of the instances are kind of the same entity and not the same entity at the same time.
They all have certain memories which are shared between all instances, but none of the instances know about each other and their experiences, the scientist's current hypothesis is that it is an entity who got way too much into character for these caricatures of people, kind of dissociating and losing its sense of self, the only evidence is that they all have certain key memories that are shared between them all, so, for now, it's quite the stretch.

Thanks for the feedback!
